subtitle: Stone that remembers the hands that raised it

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of the full Vijay Stambha rising against a burning sunset sky
panels.action: Maharana Kumbha and Sutradhar Jaita stand small yet steady at the base of the towering Vijay Stambha inside Chittor Fort, their faces upturned to the carved heights glowing in the evening light.

dialogue.text: In fifteenth‑century Chittor, Maharana Kumbha raised a victory tower to his gods and his wars—yet on its stone he carved, clear as day, the names of the men who built it.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी के चित्तौड़ में महाराणा कुम्भा ने अपने देवताओं और युद्धों के लिए विजय स्तंभ उठाया—और उसी पत्थर पर दिन की तरह साफ खुदवाए उसके बनाने वालों के नाम।

panels.shot: aerial establishing wide over Chittor Fort on a rocky hill, dawn light creeping over ramparts
panels.action: The vast spread of Chittor Fort crowns the rocky plateau, temples and palaces clustered inside its walls as pale dawn mist curls around the cliffs and ravines below.

dialogue.text: On the high rock of Chittor, where winds strip the soil to stone, the Sisodia rulers of Mewar had held out for generations against stronger, richer neighbours.

i18n.hi: चित्तौड़ की ऊँची चट्टान पर, जहाँ हवा मिट्टी तक उधेड़ दे, मेवाड़ के सिसोदिया राजाओं ने पीढ़ियों तक ताकतवर, धनवान पड़ोसियों से टक्कर ली।

panels.shot: medium interior court shot, slightly low angle on Kumbha seated in durbar, courtiers in attendance
panels.action: Inside a pillared hall, Maharana Kumbha sits upright on a low throne in a simple yet regal robe, scholars and warriors arrayed around him, his gaze intent and reflective.

dialogue.text: In the mid‑1400s, their king, Rana Kumbha, fought not only with the sword but with the pen and chisel—composer of verses, patron of temples, builder of walls and forts from Chittor to Kumbhalgarh.

i18n.hi: चौदह सौ के दशक के बीचोंबीच, उनका राजा राणा कुम्भा केवल तलवार से नहीं, कलम और छेनी से भी लड़ा—कवि, मंदिरों का संरक्षक, चित्तौड़ से कुम्भलगढ़ तक दीवारों‑किलों का निर्माता।

panels.shot: dynamic battlefield wide, slightly elevated, showing clashing armies in the distance, Kumbha on an elephant foregrounded
panels.action: On a dusty plain, armoured elephants and horsemen collide in a haze of raised dust, with Rana Kumbha standing firm atop his elephant, standard of Mewar fluttering above him as lines of soldiers press forward.

dialogue.text: The Kumbhalgarh prashasti recalls his victories—over Malwa’s sultans, over allied forces from Gujarat—campaigns whose echoes would later be carved into stone as rescued cows, broken enemy centres, and the word ‘Mleccha’ set in verse.

i18n.hi: कुम्भलगढ़ प्रशस्ति उसके विजयों को गिनाती है—मालवा के सुल्तानों पर, गुजरात की मिली‑जुली फौजों पर—ऐसे अभियान, जिनकी गूँज पत्थर पर गोधन की मुक्ति, दुश्मन के टूटे मोर्चे और पद्य में दर्ज ‘म्लेच्छ’ बनकर उभरी।

panels.shot: medium shot in a temple courtyard, Kumbha and Jaita facing each other, plans between them, low-angle hint of open sky
panels.action: In a quiet courtyard within Chittor Fort, Rana Kumbha and Sutradhar Jaita stand over a spread of palm-leaf plans, Jaita’s hand hovering above a sketched tower as Kumbha listens, temples rising behind them.

dialogue.text: From this mix of war and worship rose an idea in Chittor—a single tower that would bind victory, devotion and memory, dedicated to Vishnu yet speaking in the political language of its age.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं युद्ध और पूजा के बीच चित्तौड़ में एक ख्याल उभरा—एक ही मीनार जो विजय, भक्ति और याद को जोड़े, विष्णु को समर्पित, पर अपनी उम्र की राजनीति की भाषा बोलती।

panels.shot: close-up three-quarter on Jaita’s weathered face overlaid with a faint sketch of a tower in the foreground, soft focus background
panels.action: Sutradhar Jaita, older and sharp-eyed, leans over a palm-leaf drawing where the outline of a nine-storey tower is faintly visible, his calloused fingers steady as he imagines stone yet to rise.

dialogue.text: Jaita, master sutradhar—architect, mason, designer—took the commission. In the inscription, he will be named, along with his sons Napa, Puja and Poma, a rare honour in Indian stone.

i18n.hi: सूत्रधार जयता—स्थपति, राजमिस्त्री, डिज़ाइनर—ने काम संभाला। शिलालेख में उसका नाम आएगा, उसके बेटों नापा, पूजा और पोमा के साथ—भारतीय पत्थर पर दुर्लभ सम्मान।

panels.shot: wide construction-site shot, slightly low angle, half-built tower rising amid scaffolding and workers
panels.action: The base of the Vijay Stambha rises in fresh stone blocks wrapped in bamboo scaffolding as teams of artisans haul, chisel and measure, with Jaita guiding from below and Kumbha visiting the site surrounded by attendants.

dialogue.text: Foundation was laid around the late 1440s. Over years, perhaps a decade or more, Jaita and his lineage coaxed a nine‑storey, thirty‑seven metre tower from Chittor’s own rock.

i18n.hi: नींव चौदह सौ के दशक के आखिर में डली। कई सालों, शायद एक दशक में, जयता और उसकी वंश परंपरा ने चित्तौड़ की चट्टान से नौ मंज़िला, सैंतीस मीटर का स्तंभ निकाल लिया।

panels.shot: medium shot on Jaita’s sons on scaffolding, carving, with Jaita below, looking up, tower trunk dominating frame
panels.action: High on the scaffolding, three younger sculptors—Napa, Puja and Poma—chip intricate patterns into a panel while Jaita watches from the ground, his face a mix of scrutiny and quiet pride as the tower trunk looms above him.

dialogue.text: The inscription calls his sons by name, binding family to monument. Their hands shaped pilasters and balconies into an encyclopaedia of images—avatars of Vishnu, scenes from epics, deities, donors, even Jain figures.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख बेटों के नाम भी दर्ज करता है, परिवार को स्मारक से बाँध देता है। उनके हाथों ने खंभों और झरोखों को छवियों की किताब बना दिया—विष्णु के अवतार, महाकाव्यों के दृश्य, देवता, दानदाता, यहाँ तक कि जैन मूर्तियाँ।

panels.shot: tight vertical slice of the tower’s façade, mid-torso height, full of carved figures, with Kumbha and priests small below
panels.action: A richly carved band of the tower shows rows of deities and human figures in crisp relief, while at the base a priest gestures up to Rana Kumbha, explaining the sacred sequence as the king studies the stone.

dialogue.text: The sacred programme climbed storey by storey. The Vijay Stambha’s own verses proclaim devotion to Vishnu, invoke cow‑protection and the destruction of hostile centres, and thread politics into theology without apology.

i18n.hi: पावन योजना मंज़िल दर मंज़िल ऊपर चढ़ी। विजय स्तंभ के अपने श्लोक विष्णु भक्ति का ऐलान करते हैं, गौ‑रक्षा और शत्रु केंद्रों के विनाश का आह्वान करते हैं, और बेझिझक राजनीति को theology में पिरोते हैं।

panels.shot: interior spiral view from within the tower, looking up at winding stairs and small shrines, dim light shafting down
panels.action: Inside the tower, a tight spiral staircase wraps upward past niches holding small sculpted icons, dust motes swirling in shafts of light that fall from higher openings as a lone visitor climbs in awe.

dialogue.text: Within, narrow stairs twist past shrines and inscriptions. A visitor even today reads not a single line but layers—a record of lineage, of gods, of enemies, all caught in Sanskrit and Nagari.

i18n.hi: अंदर, सँकरी सीढ़ियाँ गर्भगृहों और लेखों के बीच लहराती हैं। आज भी यात्री एक पंक्ति नहीं, परतें पढ़ता है—वंश की, देवताओं की, दुश्मनों की—सारी की सारी संस्कृत और नागरी में कैद।

panels.shot: close-up on the inscription panel with names, viewed from over Jaita’s shoulder as he traces letters
panels.action: Over Jaita’s shoulder, the neatly incised Nagari script of the inscription runs along a smooth stone panel, his fingertip resting gently on the line that bears his own name and those of his sons.

dialogue.text: Among those lines, scholars like G.H. Ojha found the crucial verse: it names Sutradhar Jaita, and by extension Napa, Puja and Poma, letting the makers step out from the shadow of the king.

i18n.hi: इन्हीं पंक्तियों में, जी. एच. ओझा जैसे विद्वानों ने वह निर्णायक श्लोक खोजा: जो सूत्रधार जयता का नाम लेता है, और साथ ही नापा, पूजा, पोमा को, ताकि बनाने वाले राजा की छाया से बाहर आ खड़े हों।

panels.shot: medium shot, quiet moment, Kumbha and Jaita side by side at the base of the near-finished tower at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, with scaffolding largely gone, the almost-finished tower stands behind them as Rana Kumbha and Jaita stand side by side, both looking up in silence, their silhouettes framed against the stone.

dialogue.speaker: sutradhar_jaita_and_maharana_kumbha
dialogue.text: “Maharana, the stone will bear your victories. Let it also bear the hands that raised it.”

i18n.hi: “महाराणा, पत्थर आपकी जीतें ढोएगा। इसे उन हाथों को भी ढोने दो जिन्होंने इसे उठाया।”

panels.shot: low-angle shot from the base looking up, with an inscription band in foreground and Kumbha’s hand resting near it
panels.action: From the base of the tower, the camera looks up past a band of inscription where Kumbha’s hand rests lightly on the stone, the rising tiers receding into the bright sky above.

dialogue.text: The choice was conscious. The tower exalts Kumbha and his house, yet its own text fixes the sutradhar in history, making this victory pillar also a record of craft and labour.

i18n.hi: यह फैसला सोचा‑समझा था। मीनार कुम्भा और उनके घराने को महिमा देती है, पर उसका अपना शिलालेख सूत्रधार को इतिहास में कील दे देता है, इस विजय स्तंभ को शिल्प और मेहनत का भी दस्तावेज़ बना देता है।

panels.shot: modern-era wide shot, slightly desaturated, tourists as tiny figures at the base, tower dominating frame
panels.action: In a later age, small modern visitors stand craning their necks at the base of the now-weathered Vijay Stambha, their bright clothes specks of colour against the aged stone that still holds every carved figure.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, storms, sieges and neglect have passed over Chittor. Yet the Vijay Stambha stands, now a UNESCO‑noted monument, its inscriptions meticulously catalogued by epigraphists and historians.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद आँधियाँ, घेराबंदियाँ, अनदेखी सब चित्तौड़ पर गुज़र गईं। पर विजय स्तंभ अब भी खड़ा है, आज यूनेस्को की सूची में, जिसके शिलालेखों को पुरालेखविद और इतिहासकार बारीकी से दर्ज कर चुके हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on a modern scholar’s notebook and photograph of the inscription, hands comparing letters to transcription
panels.action: At a table, a scholar’s hands hold a black‑and‑white photograph of the inscription while another hand traces transliterated Nagari letters in a notebook, the names ‘Jaita’ and his sons carefully underlined.

dialogue.text: Through them we hear the tower speak. Its words still carry the sharp edge of their time—praise, polemic, piety—and among them, the clear self‑naming of craftsmen otherwise lost.

i18n.hi: उनके ज़रिए हम मीनार की आवाज़ सुनते हैं। उसके शब्द अब भी अपने समय की धार लिए हैं—स्तुति, वाद, भक्ति—और इनके बीच में कारीगरों का वह साफ‑साफ आत्म‑नाम, जो वरना खो जाते।

panels.shot: split-vision style shot: half shows Kumbha and Jaita in their era at the base; half shows a present-day visitor reading the same stone
panels.action: On one side, Kumbha and Jaita in fifteenth‑century attire stand by the fresh inscription; on the other, a present‑day visitor runs a hand over the same now‑weathered panel, the shared stone bridging their worlds.

dialogue.text: Most monuments remember only power. The Vijay Stambha remembers power in its own idiom—and, through one carved verse, also remembers the men who turned command into masonry and myth into stone.

i18n.hi: अधिकतर स्मारक सिर्फ सत्ता को याद रखते हैं। विजय स्तंभ सत्ता को अपनी ही बोली में याद रखता है—और एक खुदे हुए श्लोक के ज़रिए उन लोगों को भी, जिन्होंने हुक्म को ईंट‑पत्थर और मिथक को पत्थर की शक्ल दी।

title_i18n.hi: विजय स्तंभ ने दिया शिल्पियों को नाम

subtitle_i18n.en: Stone that remembers the hands that raised it
subtitle_i18n.hi: पत्थर जो याद रखे उठाने वाले हाथ
